t: Ibn Sa'id al-Maghribi placed the capital Wafāt on high ground in a river valley where the people grew bananas and sugar cane; al-Umari counted seven cities, an army of 20,000 soldiers and 15,000 horsemen, and a ruler who wore headbands of silk.

Sabr ad-Din's rebellion of 1332 aimed to make him king of all Ethiopia, turn the churches into mosques and set the Christian queen to grind corn; Emperor Amda Seyon destroyed Ifat's capital, looted his camp of gold and slaves, imprisoned him and installed his brother Jamal ad-Din I.

Haqq ad-Din II moved the capital to the Harar plateau and fought the emperor in more than twenty battles before dying in 1376; his brother Sa'ad ad-Din II was defeated in 1403 and killed at Zeila, after which, al-Maqrizi wrote, 'the strength of the Muslims was abated'.
dyk: When Emperor Amda Seyon threatened in 1320 to divert the Nile and starve Egypt unless the Mamluk sultan al-Nasir Muhammad stopped persecuting the Copts, the Egyptians dismissed it as an idle threat; the fear that Ethiopia might tamper with the Nile nonetheless stayed with them for centuries.
ev: Sultan Umar Walasma, founder of the dynasty, dies after carving out his kingdom and conquering the Sultanate of Shewa; 'four or five sons' rule briefly before Sabr ad-Din I.
Sultan Wali Asma imposes his rule on Hubat, Zeila and the other Muslim states of the region.
Haqq ad-Din I invades Amhara, burns churches, forces conversions and kills the emperor's envoy; Amda Seyon I raids Shewa and Ifat, and Dadader Haqq ad-Din falls at the battle of Marra Biete.
Sabr ad-Din rebels to become 'King of all Ethiopia'; Amda Seyon destroys the capital of Ifat, imprisons him and appoints Jamal ad-Din I in his place.
Haqq ad-Din II, who moved the capital to the Harar plateau and fought over twenty battles with the emperor, dies in battle; his brother Sa'ad ad-Din II succeeds.
Ifat's troops are defeated on the Harar plateau; Sa'ad ad-Din II flees to Zeila and is killed there, by al-Maqrizi's account (another source dates his death to 1410 under Emperor Yeshaq).

f.capital: Ifat (Wafāt), probably at Walalah in eastern Shewa; the Harar plateau and Zeila under Haqq ad-Din II
f.founder: Umar ibn Dunya-huz, Sultan Umar Walasma, founder of the Walashma dynasty, who died around 1275
f.predecessor: Sultanate of Shewa, conquered by Umar Walasma; the Muslim states of Gidaya, Dawaro, Bale and Fatagar
f.successor: Adal Sultanate, with its capital at Harar; the Ethiopian Empire's provinces of Yifat and Menz
